standard.title: Technology shapes text response
standard.description: Explain the effect of current technology on reading, creating and responding to texts including media texts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can examine texts including media texts and identify how they reflect the context in which they were created (AC9E6LY01). They have not yet explained the effect of current technology on reading, creating and responding — moving from identifying contextual influence to explaining technological effect.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain how current technology affects reading, creating and responding to texts.

nodes.label: Technology changes how we read and respond
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how current technologies affect how readers encounter, navigate and respond to texts
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one way that a specific technology (e.g. digital news, social media, e-readers) changes how a reader encounters or responds to a text compared to a print equivalent
nodes.typical_width: Examine how digital technologies affect reading in multiple ways — non-linear navigation, interactive elements, comment and response features, algorithmic curation — and explain the effect of each on how readers engage with texts
wider: Analyse the impact of interactive elements of digital texts — e.g. hyperlinks, comment sections, share functions — on how readers engage with and respond to digital magazines or news articles
Identify changes in topics considered newsworthy as a result of technological change — how do social media and algorithmic curation affect what counts as news?

response_modes.reason: Students commonly describe technology's effects in general terms ('it's easier', 'you can access it anywhere') without explaining specific effects on reading and response. Examining concrete technology examples across different text types — news, fiction, social media — builds the specific explanatory understanding the descriptor requires.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Algorithmic curation and changes in newsworthiness are genuinely rich territory — advancing students can investigate how technology shapes not just how we read but what gets read, connecting to media literacy and critical thinking.
success_criteria: Identifies a specific technology and explains its effect on how texts are read or responded to
The explanation goes beyond convenience to address how the technology changes the reading or response experience

nodes.label: Technology changes how we create texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how current technologies affect how texts are created, including the influence of technology on language and form
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one way that a specific technology (e.g. SMS, email, GIFs, podcasting tools) has changed how texts are created or what forms are available
nodes.typical_width: Examine how communicative technologies such as SMS, email and GIFs have influenced written language — what features of digital communication have entered broader language use? — and explain why the technology shapes the form
wider: Investigate how new digital text forms (vlogs, podcasts, interactive stories) have emerged from technological affordances — what does each technology enable that wasn't possible before?
Examine how the same communicative goal (e.g. sharing news, telling a story) is achieved differently across technological platforms and discuss what is gained and lost in each form

response_modes.reason: Students are immersed in digital text creation but rarely reflect on how technology shapes the forms they use. Examining multiple technologies and the text forms they enable — and comparing digital with non-digital forms of the same communicative goal — builds explicit understanding of the technology-form relationship.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The emergence of new digital text forms (vlogs, podcasts, interactive stories) and the comparison of the same communicative goal across platforms give advancing students genuinely rich investigative territory — connecting technological affordance to form in ways that build transferable critical awareness of how technology shapes communication.
success_criteria: Identifies a technology and explains a specific effect it has on how texts are created
Explains why the technology produces that effect on form or language
